note: RFP Builder part three: the client-ready sentences the knowledge base answers with. Each sentence lists the quotes that back it (q); build_facts.py finds every quote among the facts marked verified in hosting.json, security.json and uptime_privacy_licensing.json (or, for a quote that starts with pdf:, in the text of Adobe's Brand Concierge security overview kept in abc/internal/, or, for one that starts with trust:, in Adam's copy of Adobe's Trust Center compliance list in trust_center/), takes each source from the fact it matched, and stops if a quote is not found. 'for' names the catalog products a sentence speaks for ('*' for every Adobe product in the answer that 'only' allows). Sentences with a 'for' list are shown after the products' names; '*' sentences stand alone. 'client': false sends a sentence to the partner's note, never the response. 'own' marks the partner's own sentence, which needs no quote. 'confirm' lines go to Confirm with Adobe; 'asks' to Ask your client.

explain_note: Step 66 (Nov 10 2026): the sentences an answer opens with. "for" names the products the draft must hold; "when" lists words (matched from the start of a word) of which the question must use one, or two beside a connection; kind "what" is what a product is, used when nothing more specific fits; kind "role" is its part in a "which products" answer; "first" puts the sentence ahead of a connection's own text; "confirm" is a note for the partner only. Every sentence lists the quotes that back it (q), found by build_facts.py among the verified facts in explain.json.

explain.text: Brand Visibility measures how your brand appears in AI-generated answers, recommends content changes and tracks how that performance changes over time.
q: It provides insights into brand presence in AI-generated answers, offers prescriptive content recommendations
how that performance changes over time

explain.text: Brand Visibility measures how your brand appears in AI-generated answers.
q: It provides insights into brand presence in AI-generated answers

explain.text: Brand Visibility runs the prompts you choose on a recurring basis across the AI platforms it supports and records how your brand appears in each answer and how that changes over time. It measures the prompts you monitor: the questions people put to AI assistants themselves are not disclosed by the platforms.
q: Each prompt is executed on a recurring basis across supported AI platforms
It provides ongoing visibility measurements for the prompts you actively monitor
The exact prompts you ask LLMs are not publicly available because they are not disclosed by the LLMs.

explain.text: Adobe's Brand Presence page lists ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Perplexity as supported. The experience varies with your Brand Visibility edition, so we would confirm the platforms in yours before the baseline.
q: Adobe Brand Visibility currently supports ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Co-pilot, Google Gemini, and Perplexity.
The Brand Presence experience varies based on your Adobe Brand Visibility edition.
explain.confirm: Brand Visibility platforms: the list of six with Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot is on Adobe's Brand Presence (Trial) page; the AI Visibility page lists ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode and Gemini, and the Brand Presence (powered by Semrush) page names none. Confirm with Adobe which platforms your client's edition covers before you promise Perplexity.

explain.text: Its AI Visibility view opens the full AI answer behind a prompt: the response text, whether your brand was mentioned, which other brands were mentioned, whether your site was cited and the source URLs behind the answer.
q: opens the full AI answer behind a prompt: the response text, whether your brand was mentioned, which brands were mentioned, whether your site was cited and the source URLs behind the answer.

explain.text: The dashboards report the percentage of prompts where your brand is mentioned, how often your website is used as a source, share of voice and sentiment, and compare you with the other brands you choose to track in each market.
q: Brand Visibility measures the percentage of prompts where your brand is mentioned.
how often your website is used as a source in AI answers
Share of Voice now reflects your visibility
Sentiment is evaluated at the aspect level
Tracking other brands enables Brand Presence to compare your performance against other brands within the same market.

explain.text: Two further views cover your own site: Agentic Traffic shows how AI agents (crawlers and chatbots) interact with your pages, from your CDN logs, and Referral Traffic shows the visits from people who clicked citation links in AI-generated answers.
q: The Agentic Traffic dashboard shows how AI agents (crawlers and chatbots) interact with your site.
sourced from the CDN logs
The total traffic from human users who clicked citation links in AI-generated answers.

explain.text: Brand Concierge is Adobe's platform for conversational experiences on your website, mobile apps and other digital properties. Every conversation is grounded in your own content and guardrails.
q: launch personalized conversational experiences on their customer-facing surfaces: websites, mobile apps, and other digital properties
Every conversation is grounded in the brand

explain.text: Brand Concierge answers visitors' questions from the content you approve.
q: A concierge answers questions using only its configured knowledge sources.

explain.text: Brand Concierge answers only from the knowledge sources you configure (website pages, PDFs and product spreadsheets), not from general world knowledge. Website sources refresh on a schedule you set, so answers keep up with the pages you publish.
q: A concierge answers questions using only its configured knowledge sources. It does not answer from general world knowledge.
The three types of knowledge sources: website URLs, PDFs, and product spreadsheets
Schedule a refresh frequency, such as weekly on a specified day and time, to keep the knowledge source current as the website changes.

explain.text: When a question falls outside those sources, the concierge is designed to say it does not have the information rather than generate an unsupported answer, and guardrails can exclude topics such as legal or compliance matters.
q: the concierge is designed to indicate that it does not have the information instead of generating an unsupported answer
guardrails can exclude legal topics, compliance topics, or competitor discussions

explain.text: Brand Concierge is focused on anonymous visitors: it answers from the conversation and your knowledge sources, not from an individual customer's records. Questions about a customer's own account would go to your secure channels.
q: In the current scope, Concierge is focused on anonymous visitors: it answers from the conversation and your knowledge base (website and catalog), not from a live lookup of identity or journey state in Real-Time CDP.
explain.confirm: Brand Concierge and a customer's own account: Adobe's FAQ says the current scope is anonymous visitors, while other Adobe pages mention account information and a Real-Time CDP integration in Limited Availability. Do not promise answers about an individual customer's account until Adobe confirms it.

explain.text: Before launch, it is tested against a golden set of real customer questions paired with ideal answers, including questions it should not answer; after launch, conversation transcripts are reviewed on a recurring basis.
q: What a golden set is: real visitor questions paired with ideal answers
Checks how the concierge handles questions it should not answer
Establish a recurring process for reviewing conversation transcripts and adding new evaluation questions as they surface.

explain.text: A conversation can be handed to a person through live chat or a booked meeting without losing its context; both run on Adobe's companion product, Adobe Marketo Qualifier.
q: Live chat and meeting booking are the two ways Brand Concierge hands that conversation to a human without losing the context the visitor already provided.
These capabilities are powered by a companion product called Adobe Marketo Qualifier
explain.confirm: Brand Concierge handoff: live chat and meeting booking run on Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier), which Adobe frames as handoff to sales. Confirm with Adobe that your client has access to it and that it suits a service handoff.

explain.text: AEM Sites as a Cloud Service is built on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, with code deployed through Cloud Manager and pages edited visually in the Universal Editor.
q: The Core Components are a set of standardized Web Content Management (WCM) components for AEM
it is the sole mechanism for deploying code to AEM as a Cloud Service
The Universal Editor is a versatile visual editor that is part of Adobe Experience Manager Sites.

explain.text: We would implement AEM Sites as a Cloud Service: code is deployed through Cloud Manager, the site is built on Adobe's Core Components and page templates, and your authors edit pages visually in the Universal Editor.
q: it is the sole mechanism for deploying code to AEM as a Cloud Service
The Core Components are a set of standardized Web Content Management (WCM) components for AEM
The template defines the structure of the resultant page
The Universal Editor is a versatile visual editor that is part of Adobe Experience Manager Sites.

explain.text: How your existing content moves depends on where it sits today. From an existing AEM instance, Adobe's Content Transfer Tool moves it across. From another CMS, Adobe's importer tooling targets sites delivered on Edge Delivery Services, so we would agree the export and import route for your content in discovery.
q: can be used to initiate the migration of existing content from a source AEM instance (on-premise or AMS) to the target AEM Cloud Service instance
Supports migrations from a wide range of CMS platforms, legacy AEM, or design systems (like Figma) into production-capable Edge Delivery Services projects
The agent does not support the following targets. AEM publish environments where sites use HTL-based delivery
explain.confirm: AEM Sites migration from another CMS: Adobe documents the Content Transfer Tool for AEM sources only (AEM 6.3 or higher), and the AEM Importer and the Experience Modernization Agent for Edge Delivery Services targets only. Ask your client what the site runs on today before you size the migration.

explain.text: For go-live we would plan a content freeze for the final content top-up, test in the stage environment, which has the same sizing as production, and run user acceptance testing on a test subdomain before the DNS cutover.
q: you need to plan for a content freeze when the final content top-up is scheduled
Perform tests in a stage environment. It has the same sizing as production.
Create a test subdomain to connect your production instance to before you go-live and do a round of UAT testing.

explain.text: There are two documented routes. The simpler one: forms built in Marketo Engage are embedded on the site's pages with Marketo's own embed code, so each submission is a Marketo form fill. It runs on your Marketo Engage subscription and involves no AEM Forms license, though Marketo's form prefill does not work with the embed code.
q: Forms can reside on Marketo landing pages or be embedded on any page of your website.
Access a form
Marketo associates the cookie and all related web activity with the known lead
Form Prefill does not work when using the form embed code on your own pages or a Marketo landing page.

explain.text: The fuller one: AEM Forms adaptive forms with the Submit to Marketo Engage action, which add a rule editor, prefill, e-signatures and a PDF record of each submission. It needs an AEM Forms license as well as Marketo Engage, because AEM Sites and AEM Forms are licensed individually. We would use embedded Marketo forms for standard lead capture and adaptive forms where a form needs that logic.
q: Adaptive Forms editor provides the Submit to Marketo Engage submit action to send Adaptive Forms data to Adobe Marketo Engage for processing.
Supports a built-in Rule Editor for adding logic and conditions.
Offers a Prefill service to auto-populate form data.
integrate forms with Adobe Sign to add e-signatures to forms, and generate Document of Record (DoR) to archive submitted forms as PDF files
These services are licensed individually, but can be used in collaboration.
A valid Adobe Marketo Engage license

explain.text: Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous data from your systems together into customer profiles, builds audiences from them and activates those audiences across channels.
q: helps companies bring together known and anonymous data from multiple enterprise sources in order to create customer profiles
so that you can build profiles and define audiences
so you can seamlessly activate these audiences

explain.text: Real-Time CDP brings known and anonymous customer data together into profiles and builds the audiences.
q: helps companies bring together known and anonymous data from multiple enterprise sources in order to create customer profiles
so that you can build profiles and define audiences

explain.text: Adobe Target personalizes experiences across web, mobile and other digital channels: A/B tests compare experiences, and Experience Targeting delivers content to a specific audience by rules you define.
q: offers comprehensive tools to personalize customer experiences across web, mobile sites, apps, social media, and other digital channels
Compares two or more experiences to see which experience best improves conversions
Experience Targeting (XT) delivers content to a specific audience based on a set of marketer-defined rules and criteria.

explain.text: Target delivers the personalized experiences on the site and tests them.
q: offers comprehensive tools to personalize customer experiences across web, mobile sites, apps, social media, and other digital channels
Compares two or more experiences to see which experience best improves conversions

explain.text: Customer Journey Analytics brings Analysis Workspace to the data in Adobe Experience Platform, so journeys can be analyzed across channels in one reporting view.
q: lets you use the power of Analysis Workspace with data from Adobe Experience Platform
Data from your call center, POS systems, and online properties can be combined into a single reporting view.

explain.text: Customer Journey Analytics measures the results across channels.
q: You can view and analyze data sequentially, spanning multiple channels.

explain.text: A customer becomes known when they sign in: the site sends a person-level identifier, such as a CRM ID, with the visit, and Experience Platform stitches it into their profile.
q: When a visitor signs in, completes a purchase, or otherwise becomes known, you can send person-level identifiers (CRM ID, hashed email, loyalty ID, etc.) alongside the ECID.
Identity stitching (ID stitching) is the process of identifying data fragments and combining them together to form a complete profile record.

explain.text: Real-Time CDP's Adobe Target destination makes those audiences available to Target for same-page and next-page personalization, with governance and privacy support, using a datastream.
q: The Adobe Target destination in Real-Time CDP allows you to use Experience Platform segments in Adobe Target for same page-personalization and next-page personalization with governance and privacy support.
you must use a datastream when configuring the Adobe Target connection

explain.text: Results are measured in Customer Journey Analytics, used as the reporting source for Target's A/B activities: its Experimentation panel compares the variations and reports each one's lift over the baseline, and the confidence in it, on the success metrics you choose.
q: To use Customer Journey Analytics as the reporting source for Target
The Experimentation panel lets analysts compare different user experiences, marketing, or messaging variations to determine which is best at driving a specific outcome.
You can evaluate the lift and confidence of any A/B experiment
The Experiment report summary shows the Lift over Baseline
explain.confirm: Target reporting in Customer Journey Analytics: it covers A/B activities; Auto-Target and Automated Personalization do not yet support Customer Journey Analytics as the reporting source, and Automated Personalization and Recommendations need Target Premium. Check which activity types your client wants before you promise this reporting for them.

explain.text: Consent and data-use rules travel with the data: the Web SDK sends or discards data according to each visitor's consent, and Experience Platform enforces the data usage policies you enable when audiences are activated.
q: The setConsent command tells the Web SDK if it should send data (opt in), discard data (opt out), or use defaultConsent (consent unknown).
Experience Platform automatically enforces usage policies should any violations occur when activating audiences to destinations
